problem_description: Compute the average of shear stress in bar of a 3D metallic crystal system (nickel) using the MEAM potential (specifically the Ni4 parameterization). The system is constructed as a face-centered cubic (FCC) lattice with lattice constant 3.52 Å with a crystalline orientation of [1 0 0] along x, [0 1 1] along y, and [0 -1 1] along z, and an origin shift of 0.5 along x, in a simulation box (16*10*2.828427 A^3 (in metal units)) that is periodic along the z-direction and non-periodic (shrink-wrapped) along x and y. Atoms are divided into three regions: lower and upper boundary layers, and a central mobile region (0.9 and 6.1 specify the y-coordinate boundaries that separate the lower region (y ≤ 0.9) and the upper region (y ≥ 6.1), respectively, while all other directions are left unbounded using INF.). The boundary atoms are kept frozen (or fixed) by setting their forces to zero. Initial velocities are assigned corresponding to a temperature of 300 K, and the system is equilibrated for 100 steps using a 1 fs timestep under the NVE ensemble for boundary atoms while a velocity rescaling thermostat (temp/rescale) is applied to mobile atoms. The shear deformation is introduced by setting the upper boundary to a constant velocity (1 A/ps) in the x-direction, while the linear velocity gradient is applied to the mobile atoms (0 to 1 A/ps) along the y-direction (1.4 to 8.6 A). To ensure the accurate thermal control under shear, the existing thermostat is removed and replaced with a velocity-rescaling thermostat that maintains the system at 300 K by utilizing a partial temperature compute (temp/partial 0 1 1) that calculates the temperature only from the y and z velocity components to remove the streaming x-velocity bias. The system is evolved for 5000 timesteps. The shear stress is dumping every 1000 steps using the compute stress/atom.
